body:
Triage note (half-state, same shape as #9748): this card carries `pm:blocked`, but neither the body nor any comment holds a machine-readable `Blocked-by: #N` line — the unlock scan can never release it. To the filing seat: please add `Blocked-by: #<n>` (a comment is fine, per the body-escaping trap) naming the actual upstream — PR #9750's merge? #9747's direction ruling? — or drop the label if it is not actually waiting on anything. First-touch grading is deferred until the line lands; on its face the card reads queue-ready (ruled B by the lane PM, with the population-pricing steps already in the card).

---

## PM seat action (#10021) — re-graded `pm:blocked` → `pm:queue`

Re-graded to `pm:queue`. The body's only upstream reference is **#9747** — *"this is the **sink-TYPE axis** of that card"* — and **#9747 is CLOSED** (shipped as PR #9875, the `UNRECOGNISED` third exit state). So whatever dependency existed is discharged.

⚠️ Carry forward from #9747's ruling when this is dispatched: the family answer was **visibility-only, no new merge-blocking context**, and this card's own body already agrees (*"⛔ Not a new required context; this argues for a producer-side constraint, not more merge-blocking"*). Those two are consistent — good.

---

**Why there was nothing to backfill.** #10021 asked for either a machine-readable `Blocked-by: #<n>` line or a re-grade. Auditing all five cards it names, **none carries a real issue dependency** — `pm:blocked` was applied as a *holding state*, not as an edge. That is the honest answer to the escalation: the label was wrong, not the `Blocked-by:` line missing. A backfill would have invented edges to satisfy a scan.

⚠️ Worth recording: the unlock scan's grep *did* report hits on two of the five — but they were the literal template text `Blocked-by: #N` / `Blocked-by: #<n>` inside the triage comment **asking for one**. A scan that matches the instruction to add an edge, and reports it as an edge, is the same false-green family this lane has worked all day.

**PM note (`domain:devx` seat) — not a claim.** Recording two measurements taken while gating this card, so they are not re-derived later.

**1. Serial hold stands, behind PR #10396 (#9748).** Confirmed by *declaration site*, not by the card's filenames:

| symbol | declared at | edited by #10396 |
|---|---|---|
| `SweepLogger` | `packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/outbox-sweep.ts:93` | ✅ yes |
| `ProjectionLogger` | `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-set-projection.ts:93` | ✅ yes |

Both types are declared *inside* the two files #10396 rewrites, so this is **serial, not parallel**. #10396 currently has a live merge-queue ref; this unblocks when it lands.

⛔ And still **not a fold with #9748**, on gate ①: #9748 is a *call-site spelling* (`logger?.error?.(…)` emitting nothing against an `error`-less sink), this is the *type contract*. Same files, different defect form and different fix.

**2. ⚠️ The file surface is wider than this card names.** `ProjectionLogger` is imported by two further files that #10396 does **not** touch:

- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/bootstrap-declared-capabilities.ts:59`
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/bootstrap-declared-permissions.ts:45`

So a change to `ProjectionLogger`'s contract propagates to at least **four** source files plus the two `.test.ts` siblings, not the two this card lists. Whoever takes it should size it from that surface and re-check it themselves — this is a reading of `origin/main` at 19:0xZ, not a promise about the tree at claim time.

NOTE ON REBUILD: neither ablation involves dist/ — the checker is a source scanner and the tsc pin is read by `tsc --noEmit` over src/, so there is no stale-dist path to defeat; the pre-flight that applies here is the on-disk anchor count, which was done on every limb. (5) Gate union re-derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` (no path args, three-dot from merge base, 8 paths) and run at 4d7374f8a9, each exit captured with `EXIT=$?` after redirect (never after a pipe): check:optional-error-sink 0 (self-test: 13 cases, both directions, both narrowings pinned as counts), check:nul-bytes 0, check:type-check-coverage 0, check:cross-package-test-inputs 0, check:test-source-alias 0, check:engine-double-contract 0, check:where-matcher 0, check:query-options-erasure 0, check:i18n 0, check:changeset-gate-self-tests 0, check:objectui-changeset 0, check:slot-lookup 0, check:type-source-resolution 0, check-adr-0087-registration 0, check-changeset-no-major 0, check-empty-changeset 0, check-affected-docs 0. (6) DECLARED NARROWING: `check:type-check-debt --re-measure` was NOT run locally (it needs the whole workspace closure built); neither edited package is a ledger entry — both declare a `typecheck` script — so this diff cannot move that ratchet, and CI runs it. (7) A REAL DEFECT THE GATES CAUGHT IN MY OWN DIFF: `check:type-check-coverage` reddened on a `@ts-expect-error` I had put in plugin-security's test file — that package's tsconfig excludes `**/*.test.ts`, so the directive would evaluate NEVER (phantom pin). Removed, with the reason recorded in the test; the compile-time pin lives in plugin-email, whose package does compile its tests, and its liveness is what ablation 2 demonstrates. `check:i18n` first reported PREREQUISITE NOT MET (the workspace CLI was unbuilt — 'Nothing was checked'); after `turbo run build --filter=@objectstack/cli` it is green (9 packages in sync).",
```json
  "open_questions": [
    {
      "question": "Should `pnpm check:optional-error-sink` be wired into CI, and where? The card forbids more merge-blocking (\"⛔ Not a new required context; this argues for a producer-side constraint, not more merge-blocking\"), and #9747's family ruling was visibility-only — but every `check:*` gate in this repo lives in the required `Lint & Repo Gates` job, so 'wired' and 'merge-blocking' are the same thing here. Left UNWIRED in PR #10555, stated in the gate header and the PR body. Mechanically forced too: `.github/workflows/lint.yml` is open PR #10506's file surface, which this dispatch told me to stay out of.",
      "options": [
        "A: leave it unwired and on-demand (current state) — honest to the card, but a gate nobody runs is dormant, which is the declared-not-enforced shape AGENTS.md #10 warns about",
        "B: add a step to the existing required `Lint & Repo Gates` job after #10506 lands — no NEW required context (the check-run name is unchanged), but it does add merge-blocking inside one",
        "C: give it a report-only lane of its own (the `engine-split-metric.yml` shape) — visibility without blocking, at the cost of a new workflow file and a signal nobody has to read"
      ],
      "recommendation": "B, after #10506 lands, with the ledger as the safety valve: the 15 pre-existing reds are already baselined, so wiring it can only red on a NEWLY written silence-permitting sink — which is exactly the class the card wants to stop existing, and is a one-line fix when it fires. C is the literal reading of 'visibility-only', but this repo has no habit of reading advisory lanes, so it buys the appearance of enforcement rather than enforcement. If the lane PM prefers to hold the card's constraint strictly, A is stable — the checker is runnable and its census is useful on demand — but then say so on #9754 so 'not wired' is a recorded decision rather than an oversight."
    },
    {
      "question": "Is `minor` the right bump for tightening an exported sink type on two published packages?",
      "options": [
        "A: minor (chosen) — an optional member becoming required can break an external TS caller, and `major` is banned by check:changeset-no-major",
        "B: patch — matches PR #10396's sibling fix on the same two files, and no in-repo caller is affected (verified: no call sites outside the two packages)"
      ],
      "recommendation": "A. No in-repo consumer breaks, but `ProjectionDeps` is exported from `@objectstack/plugin-security`'s index, so an external host passing a `warn`-less sink does break, and the changeset body carries the one-line fix. Both packages sit in the `fixed` group, so this bumps the group's minor — flagging it in case the lane PM would rather batch such tightenings."
    }
  ],
  "out_of_scope_findings": [
    "filed as #10556: pay down the optional-error sink ledger — 15 sink types still declare an `error` that can go nowhere; 13 are a one-line `warn?` -> `warn` repair (two of them plugin-audit's, held only by open PR #10450's file surface), and two are design calls: plugin-security's own logger field is initialised `= {}` (its default sink prints nothing at all), and service-settings' `SettingsDiagnosticsLogger` is `{ error? }` with no alternative whatsoever — the only `no-fallback` sink left in the tree. The issue also records the 16th red sink in `examples/**` (outside the checker's deliberate `packages/**` scope) and the fact that plugin-security hides its tests from tsc, so a type pin there is a phantom."
  ]
}
```
